en.title: Extraordinary Attorney Woo's Japanese Remake 'Minami' Lands October 2026 Netflix Date
en.summary: Fans craving more of the beloved legal drama can mark their calendars for a fresh take. The Japanese adaptation, 'Extraordinary Attorney Minami,' is set to premiere on Netflix.
en.body:
While the wait for the second season of the critically acclaimed **Extraordinary Attorney Woo** continues, a delightful new way to experience the series is on the horizon. Netflix has officially announced the Japanese adaptation, titled **Extraordinary Attorney Minami**, will begin streaming weekly new episodes on October 18, 2026. This reimagining brings the compelling story of a brilliant autistic lawyer to a new audience, featuring **Ashida Mana** in the lead role as Minamida Minami.

Like its Korean predecessor, **Extraordinary Attorney Minami** will follow the journey of a gifted lawyer who, despite graduating at the top of her class and passing the bar exam with flying colors, must navigate societal prejudice and prove her capabilities in the challenging legal world. The series is directed by **Miyake Yoshishige** and, while not a Netflix Original, has secured a distribution deal with the platform for audiences outside of Japan. Local Japanese broadcast on Fuji TV is scheduled to begin on October 19, 2026, with Netflix's release date expected to align closely.

## A Familiar Story, A New Perspective

The adaptation promises to capture the heartwarming and thought-provoking essence of the original series. The synopsis highlights Minamida Minami's exceptional intellect and her triumph over the bar exam, juxtaposed with the societal barriers she encounters as she seeks employment. This narrative arc, central to **Extraordinary Attorney Woo**'s success, is expected to resonate with viewers who appreciate stories of overcoming adversity and challenging preconceptions. The series is set to run for ten episodes, each approximately 54 minutes long, offering a substantial binge-watching opportunity for dedicated fans.

## Why This Matters to Fans

For fans of **Extraordinary Attorney Woo**, this Japanese remake offers a chance to engage with the character and themes they love in a new cultural context. Adaptations can often spark lively discussions within fan communities about how different creative teams interpret and translate beloved narratives. The casting of **Ashida Mana**, a well-regarded actress in Japan, adds another layer of anticipation. Viewers will be keen to see her portrayal of Minamida Minami and how the Japanese legal system and societal nuances are woven into the familiar plot.

## What's Next

With a confirmed Netflix release date of October 18, 2026, fans can anticipate the first episode to drop on that day, followed by weekly installments. The dual release across Netflix and Fuji TV ensures broad accessibility for both international and domestic audiences. Further details regarding specific case storylines and any potential creative departures from the original will likely emerge closer to the premiere date.

Extraordinary Attorney Minami is an upcoming Japanese legal drama directed by Miyake Yoshishige, an adaptation of the beloved Korean drama Extraordinary Attorney Woo .  The series is not a Netflix Original, but has been licensed to Netflix for distribution outside Japan. When is Extraordinary Attorney Minami coming to Netflix? Extraordinary Attorney Minami is officially slated to hit Netflix on October 18, 2026. However, since the local Japanese broadcast begins on October 19, Netflix’s exact release date may shift slightly to align with it. There will be a total of ten episodes, with a new episode released weekly on Netflix and broadcast on Fuji TV. Episodes will have an approximate runtime of 54 minutes. What is the plot of Extraordinary Attorney Minami ? The full synopsis for Extraordinary Attorney Minami has been sourced from MyDramaList: Minamida Minami, who has autism spectrum disorder (ASD), graduates at the top of her class from the University of Tokyo’s Faculty of Law and also achieves the highest score on the bar examination. However, when she begins searching for a job, she runs up against the barrier of society’s prejudice toward people with autism spectrum disorder. Despite her outstanding credentials, she is unable to secure a position at any law firm. Then, for a certain reason, she is hired by Hirokawa & Howard Law Firm, one of the top firms in the industry. However, because Minami has difficulty reading other people’s emotions and communicating with them, as well as adapting to unexpected situations, those around her view her with prejudice, believing that there is no way she could possibly deal directly with clients. Minami herself is also uncertain whether she is capable of working as a lawyer. Even so, armed with her love of the law and her extraordinary memory, and with the help of her colleagues, she takes on one difficult case after another. At the same time, a succession of events that profoundly shake Minami’s life awaits her, including experiencing romantic feelings for the first time and discovering secrets hidden within her family….
